craft_notes: Sthāyin: wonder at unknowable workings. Device: end-dash→comma (fruit stated softly, gauging released). Atarkya kept: no explanation of HOW will fruits worlds. Rejected: 'wishing' for 'resolve' — killed: icchā is will, not wish. Read aloud: lands on close.

lines: This triple orb from bare resolve alone bears fruit,
who gauges, Lord, the orbit of thy workings?
l4.sanskrit_cite: icchāyā eva yasyeyat phalaṃ lokatrayātmakam tasya te nātha kāryāṇāṃ ko vetti kiyatī gatiḥ

reads_against.argmap: Of will alone: of whom this-much fruit, three-world-constituted.; Of him, of you, O lord — of works who knows how great the reach? (Vṛtti M00089: icchāmātreṇa, atarkya beyond reckoning). → Mere will fruits as three worlds; your works' reach is unknowable.
c1_essence: Mere will fruits as three worlds; workings reach past knowing; work-stair climbed by Brahmā.
reads_against.l2: This whole of three worlds fruits from mere will of yours alone — who, O lord, knows the reach of your workings?
l3: This triple orb from bare resolve alone bears fruit —
who gauges, Lord, the orbit of thy workings?
reads_against.t1: Of whose mere will this three-world-whole is the fruit — who knows, O lord, how far your works reach?
